ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p9/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p9/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p9/r4.claim: Eloquent Arabic suppresses the parallel clause: whether speech is open or secret, God knows what is hidden and still more hidden.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p9/r4.anchor: parallel portion of the verse are suppressed because of concomitant indications.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p9/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p9/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p9/r5.claim: The Prophet is reassured that God hears his pleadings in any state in which he voices them.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p9/r5.anchor: all his pleadings to God are heard by Him in whatever state he utters them.

QASHANI:20:6-12/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:20:6-12/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:20:6-12/r2.claim: God's knowledge penetrates outward, inward, secret, and most hidden; He knows whether speech is loud or quiet.
QASHANI:20:6-12/r2.anchor: بيان لكمال لطفه أي: علمه نافذ في الكل يعلم ظواهرها وبواطنها والسر وسر السر

NAHHAS:v3p33/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p33/r2.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p33/r2.claim: The condition is jussive, with its answer فإنه يعلم السر وأخفى; وأخفى means “more hidden than it.”
NAHHAS:v3p33/r2.anchor: مجزوم بالشرط والجواب ( فإنه يعلم السر وأخفى ) أي وأخفى منه

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p10/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p10/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p10/r1.claim: Because God knows everything hidden and open, He will ease the Prophet's path and guide him; any delay serves a reason and his benefit.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p10/r1.anchor: when his Lord is aware of all his secrets, his path would be eased out by Him

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p313/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p313/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p313/r2.claim: The address “if you speak aloud” apparently concerns the Messenger, though it may address his community; mentioning the secret implies the louder is known too.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p313/r2.anchor: والخطاب بقوله: وإن تجهر بالقول للرسول ظاهر أو المراد أمته

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p313/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p313/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p313/r3.claim: Akhfā is apparently the superlative “more hidden”; Ibn ʿAbbās gives two accounts of sirr and akhfā, while Mujāhid says akhfā is the inner whisper.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p313/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس: السر ما تسره إلى غيرك، والأخفى ما تخفيه في نفسك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p313/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p313/r4.speaker: ابن زيد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p313/r4.claim: Ibn Zayd says sirr belongs to creatures and the most hidden is God’s own secret; al-Ṭabarī rejects this.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p313/r4.anchor: وقال ابن زيد السر؟؟؟ لخلائق وأخفى منه سره تعالى وأنكر ذلك الطبري

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p313/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p313/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p313/r5.claim: Other views make sirr a settled intention and akhfā what has not entered the heart, or a past verb; parallels are cited from 2:255 and 20:110.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p313/r5.anchor: وقيل: السر العزيمة وأخفى منه ما لم يخطر على القلب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p313/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p313/r6.speaker: الزمخشري وابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p313/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya calls the past-tense interpretation weak; al-Zamakhsharī says the verse may discourage loud invocation as in 7:205 or teach its other purpose.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p313/r6.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: وليس بذلك قال: فإن قلت: كيف طابق الجزاء الشرط

BIQAI-FULL:v5p12/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p12/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p12/r1.claim: Moses's experience of forgetting and later being guided, his prayer for eloquence, and his plea for a helper model the Prophet's prayer for a minister; God aided him through Umar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p12/r1.anchor: فأيده بأعظم ويزير : عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه

BIQAI-FULL:v5p12/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p12/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p12/r2.claim: The completion of Moses's story rebukes Jews who taught Quraysh to ask Muhammad about the Spirit: it includes details unknown to them, such as the festival day, magicians' faith, threatened crucifixion, and the Samaritan's use of the messenger's trace.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p12/r2.anchor: منها أن الموعد كان يوم الزينة , ومنها إيمان السحرة

ELMALILI:20:7-9/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:20:7-9/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:20:7-9/r1.claim: Elmalılı first takes “sirr” as what one tells oneself and “ahfā” as what is still yet to occur.
ELMALILI:20:7-9/r1.anchor: “Sır” içinden kendine söylediğin, “ahfâ” olacak fakat henüz olmamış bulunandır.

ELMALILI:20:7-9/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:20:7-9/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:20:7-9/r2.claim: Alternatively, “sirr” is what one whispers secretly to another, while “ahfā” is what one conceals within oneself.
ELMALILI:20:7-9/r2.anchor: Yahut “sır” başkasına gizli söylediğin, “ahfâ” nefsinde gizlediğindir.

ELMALILI:20:7-9/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:20:7-9/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:20:7-9/r3.claim: He also reports a past-tense reading of “ahfā”: God knows creatures’ secrets but has hidden His own.
ELMALILI:20:7-9/r3.anchor: Bir de “ahfâ” fi‘l-i mâzî olmak üzere mâna verilmiştir, yani kulların sırrını bilir, kendi sırrını ise gizlemiştir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:5/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:5/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:5/r6.claim: God’s knowledge of every being and event in the universe, with nothing hidden from Him, is the clearest sign of this absolute sovereignty.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:5/r6.anchor: Belirtilen mutlak egemenliğin en açık göstergesi, Allah’ın kâinattaki her varlık ve olayın bilgisine sahip olması ve hiçbir şeyin O’na gizli kalmamasıdır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:5/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:5/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:5/r7.claim: To convey how deeply divine knowledge penetrates every detail, the verse mentions both what is concealed and what is still more hidden.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:5/r7.anchor: İlâhî bilginin bütün inceliklere ve ayrıntılara nüfuz derecesini iyi kavramamız için, sadece saklananlara değinilmekle yetinilmeyip daha gizli olanlara ayrıca temas edilmiştir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:5/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:5/r8.speaker: Bazı müfessirler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:5/r8.claim: Some commentators understand what is more hidden than a secret as a person’s inward thoughts that are never expressed outwardly.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:5/r8.anchor: Bazı müfessirlere göre “sırdan daha gizli olan”ın anlamı “kişinin içinden geçirip dış dünyaya yansıtmadıkları”dır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:5/r9.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:5/r9.speaker: Taberî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:5/r9.claim: Tabari prefers the interpretation that what is more hidden than a secret is what God keeps from His servants: possible things not yet brought into existence, unknown to people except those God informs.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:5/r9.anchor: Taberî bu konudaki görüşleri verdikten sonra kendi tercih ettiği yorumu şöyle belirtir: “Sırdan daha gizli olan, Allah’ın kullarından sakladığı, var olması imkân dahilinde bulunmakla birlikte

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:5/r10.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:5/r10.speaker: M. Esed
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:5/r10.claim: Esed interprets this as God knowing not only a person’s unspoken conscious thoughts but also what happens in the unconscious.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:5/r10.anchor: M. Esed ise âyetin bu kısmını, “O sadece insanın dile getirilmeyen bilinçli düşüncelerini değil, bilinç altında olup bitenleri de bilmektedir” şeklinde açıklar

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:5/r11.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:5/r11.speaker: Tasavvufçular
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:5/r11.claim: Sufis order the spiritual depths of a person as heart, secret, spirit, hidden, and most hidden, drawing the sequence from verses that contain these terms.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:5/r11.anchor: Tasavvufçular insanın mânevî varlığını derinliğe doğru “kalp, sır, ruh, hafî, ahfâ” şeklinde sıralarken (bk. H. Kâmil Yılmaz, s. 460), bu kelimelerin geçtiği âyetlere dayanmışlardır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:5/r12.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:5/r12.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:5/r12.claim: This account implies that God knows even the deepest and most concealed dimensions of the human being, the essence of the universe.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:5/r12.anchor: Buna göre Allah, kâinatın özü olan insanın en derin ve en gizli boyutlarını da bilmektedir.

BURSEVI:v5p282#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p282#2/r1.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v5p282#2/r1.claim: The Najmī commentary defines sirr as a subtle faculty between heart and spirit, the source of spiritual secrets, and khafī as a subtler faculty between spirit and the divine presence, receiving lordly lights.
BURSEVI:v5p282#2/r1.anchor: السر باصطلاح أهل التحقيق لطيفة بين القلب والروح وهو معدن أسرار الروحانية والخفي لطيفة بين الروح والحضرة الإلهية

BURSEVI:v5p282#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p282#2/r2.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v5p282#2/r2.claim: The mention of God after “He knows the secret and what is more hidden” signals that divine attributes manifest in khafī, the subtler and more honored faculty; this is Adam’s reality and the meaning of God’s self-disclosure in him.
BURSEVI:v5p282#2/r2.anchor: ولهذا قال عقيب قوله : {يعلم السر وأخفى * الله لا إله إلا هو} الآية إشارة إلى أن مظهر ألوهية صفاته العليا

BURSEVI:v5p282#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p282#2/r3.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v5p282#2/r3.claim: The sirr exists in every person from the first creation, while khafī emerges in the second; all may bear spiritual rational truths, but only a faithful monotheist hosts divine lights, unveiling, and inspired knowledge.
BURSEVI:v5p282#2/r3.anchor: لطيفة السر التي بين القلب والروح تكون موجودة في كل إنسان عند نشأته الأولى والخفي ينتشيء عند نشأته الأخرى

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p264/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p264/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p264/r1.claim: God knows the secret and what is still more hidden.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p264/r1.anchor: وإن تجهر بالقول فإنه يعلم السر وأخفى

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p264/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p264/r2.speaker: الحسن
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p264/r2.claim: Al-Hasan says the secret is what a person confides to another, while what is more hidden is what the person keeps within.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p264/r2.anchor: قال الحسن: "السر": ما أسر الرجل إلى غيره، "وأخفى" من ذلك: ما أسر من نفسه.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p264/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p264/r3.speaker: ابن عباس، سعيد بن جبير
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p264/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas and Sa'id ibn Jubayr say the secret is what one conceals inwardly; the more hidden is future thought God places in one's heart before one knows it will occur.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p264/r3.anchor: وعن ابن عباس، وسعيد بن جبير: "السر" ما تسر في نفسك "وأخفى" من السر: ما يلقيه الله عز وجل في قلبك من بعد

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p264/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p264/r4.speaker: ابن عباس عن علي بن أبي طلحة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p264/r4.claim: In the report through Ali ibn Abi Talha, Ibn Abbas defines the hidden as what a person does not yet know he will do.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p264/r4.anchor: وقال علي بن أبي طلحة عن ابن عباس: "السر": ما أسر ابن آدم في نفسه، "وأخفى" ما خفي عليه مما هو فاعله قبل أن يعلمه.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p264/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p264/r5.speaker: مجاهد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p264/r5.claim: Mujahid says the secret is work concealed from people and the more hidden is whispering.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p264/r5.anchor: وقال مجاهد: "السر" العمل الذي تسرون من الناس، "وأخفى": الوسوسة.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p264/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p264/r6.speaker: unnamed view
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p264/r6.claim: Another view takes the secret as a firm intention and the more hidden as a thought that has not become a firm intention.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p264/r6.anchor: وقيل: "السر": هو العزيمة ["وأخفى": ما يخطر على القلب ولم يعزم عليه.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p264/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p264/r7.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p264/r7.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam says God knows people's secrets but has kept His own secret from them so that no one knows it.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p264/r7.anchor: أي يعلم أسرار العباد، وأخفى سره من عباده، فلا يعلمه أحد

BIQAI-FULL:v5p10/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p10/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p10/r1.claim: Divine sovereignty is perfectly ordered because God comprehends all; human rulers often lose knowledge of distant parts of their realm, and that ignorance disrupts rule.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p10/r1.anchor: ولما كان الملك لا ينتظم غاية الانتظام إلا بإحاطة العلم

BIQAI-FULL:v5p10/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p10/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p10/r2.claim: God already knows what is recited aloud, so reciters need not raise their voices for His sake; loudness is fitting when commanded to make others hear.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p10/r2.anchor: فلا يتكلف ذلك في غير ما أمرت بالجهر به لغرض غير الإسماع

BIQAI-FULL:v5p10/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p10/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p10/r3.claim: The secret is what two people whisper privately in fear; the more hidden includes unexpressed thoughts and unseen matters known only to God, including future intentions.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p10/r3.anchor: وهو ما يناجي به الثنان مخافته

BIQAI-FULL:v5p10/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p10/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p10/r4.claim: God's hidden knowledge includes what minds imagine but do not express, other unseen matters no one else knows, and future intentions.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p10/r4.anchor: من ذلك , وهو ما في الضمائر مما تخيلته الأفكار ولم يبرز إلى الخارج

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p37/r19.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p37/r19.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p37/r19.claim: The address to Muhammad applies to all people: when humans speak aloud to others or their idols, God knows the secret and what is still more hidden.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p37/r19.anchor: فالمخاطبة ب تجهر لمحمد عليه السلام وهي مراد بها جميع الناس إذ هي آية اعتبار

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p37/r20.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p37/r20.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p37/r20.claim: One group takes the secret as quiet speech, such as a quiet prayer recitation, and what is more hidden as inner thought.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p37/r20.anchor: فقالت فرقة السر هو الكلام الخفي الخافت كقراءة السر في الصلاة، و «الأخفى» هو ما في النفس

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p37/r21.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p37/r21.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p37/r21.claim: Another group takes the secret as present inner thought and the more hidden as what will arise within later.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p37/r21.anchor: وقالت فرقة هو ما في النفس متحصلا، و «الأخفى» هو ما سيكون فيها في المستأنف

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p37/r22.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p37/r22.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p37/r22.claim: A third group defines the secret by what human minds can contain, including possible future thoughts, and the more hidden as divine knowledge inaccessible to humans.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p37/r22.anchor: وقالت فرقة السر هو ما في نفوس البشر وكل ما يمكن أن يكون فيها في المستأنف بحسب الممكنات من معلومات البشر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p37#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p37#2/r1.speaker: بعض السلف
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p37#2/r1.claim: A reading attributed to some early authorities makes wa-akhfā a past-tense verb; the author calls this weak.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p37#2/r1.anchor: وقد تؤول على بعض السلف أنه جعل وأخفى فعلا ماضيا وهذا ضعيف،

JISHUMI:v6p4628/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4628/r13.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4628/r13.claim: Jahr is raising the voice; a voiced sound is the opposite of a whispered one.
JISHUMI:v6p4628/r13.anchor: والجهر: رفع الصوت، جهر جهرا، والصوت مجهور، ونقيضه: المهموس.

MUQATIL:20:5-8/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:20:5-8/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:20:5-8/r3.claim: God knows what people say aloud, what they hide within themselves, and what they do without knowing that He knows it.
MUQATIL:20:5-8/r3.anchor: يعني ما أسر العبد في نفسه { و } ما { وأخفى } [آية: 7] من السر، مالا يعلم أنه يعلمه، وهو عامله

QURTUBI-FULL:20:6-8/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:6-8/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:20:6-8/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas says the secret is what one tells another privately, while the more hidden is what one keeps within oneself.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:6-8/r7.anchor: قال ابن عباس: السر ما حدث به الإنسان غيره في خفاء، وأخفى منه ما أضمر في نفسه مما لم يحدث به غيره.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:6-8/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:6-8/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:20:6-8/r8.claim: In another gloss, the secret is present self-talk and the more hidden is future self-talk; people do not know tomorrow's thoughts, but God knows both today's and tomorrow's.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:6-8/r8.anchor: وعنه أيضا: السر حديث نفسك، وأخفى من السر ما ستحدث به نفسك مما لم يكن وهو كائن

QURTUBI-FULL:20:6-8/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:6-8/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:20:6-8/r9.claim: Ibn Abbas also says the secret is what a person conceals, and the more hidden is what he will do without knowing it; God knows past and future alike, with all creatures as one to His knowledge.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:6-8/r9.anchor: وقال ابن عباس أيضا: «السر» ما أسر ابن آدم في نفسه، { وأخفى } ما خفي على ابن آدم مما هو فاعله وهو لا يعلمه، فالله تعالى يعلم ذلك كله

QURTUBI-FULL:20:6-8/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:6-8/r10.speaker: قتادة وغيره
QURTUBI-FULL:20:6-8/r10.claim: Qatada and others say the secret is what a person hides inwardly and the more hidden is what has not yet happened or been conceived by anyone.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:6-8/r10.anchor: وقال قتادة وغيره: «السر» ما أضمره الإنسان في نفسه، «وأخفى» منه ما لم يكن ولا أضمره أحد.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:6-8/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:6-8/r11.speaker: ابن زيد
QURTUBI-FULL:20:6-8/r11.claim: Ibn Zayd says the secret belongs to creatures and the more hidden is God's own secret.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:6-8/r11.anchor: وقال ابن زيد: «السر» سر الخلائق، «وأخفى» منه سره عز وجل

QURTUBI-FULL:20:6-8/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:6-8/r12.speaker: الطبري
QURTUBI-FULL:20:6-8/r12.claim: Al-Tabari rejects Ibn Zayd's reading; the more hidden is what is not yet in a person's thoughts but will enter them, as Ibn Abbas says.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:6-8/r12.anchor: وأنكر ذلك الطبري، وقال: إن الذي هو «أخفى» ما ليس في سر الإنسان وسيكون في نفسه كما قال ابن عباس.

TAB-FULL:v16p13/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p13/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p13/r1.claim: Whether the Prophet speaks aloud or privately, God knows the secret held within before it is shown by bodily action or spoken aloud.
TAB-FULL:v16p13/r1.anchor: فإنه لا يخفى عليه ما استسررته في نفسك، فلم تبده بجوارحك ولم تتكلم بلسانك

TAB-FULL:v16p13/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p13/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v16p13/r2.claim: One report says the secret is what a person has done, while the still more hidden is what God places in the heart but the person does not do.
TAB-FULL:v16p13/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس، {يعلم السر وأخفى} [طه: 7] قال: السر: ما عملته أنت وأخفى: ما قذف الله في قلبك مما لم تعمله

TAB-FULL:v16p13/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p13/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v16p13/r3.claim: Another report says the secret is what a person conceals and the more hidden is what they will do before doing it; God's knowledge of past and future is one, as if all people were one soul.
TAB-FULL:v16p13/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله {يعلم السر وأخفى} [طه: 7] قال: السر: ما أسر ابن آدم في نفسه. وأخفى: قال: ما أخفى ابن آدم مما هو فاعله قبل أن يعمله

TAB-FULL:v16p13/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p13/r4.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
TAB-FULL:v16p13/r4.claim: He says the secret is what a person hides within, and the more hidden is what the person does not know will occur.
TAB-FULL:v16p13/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس: السر: ما أسر الإنسان في نفسه، وأخفى: ما لا يعلم الإنسان مما هو كائن

TAB-FULL:v16p13/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p13/r5.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v16p13/r5.claim: He identifies the more hidden as whispering and the secret as a deed people conceal from others.
TAB-FULL:v16p13/r5.anchor: عن مجاهد، في قول الله: {يعلم السر وأخفى} [طه: 7] قال: أخفى: الوسوسة

TABATABAI:20:1-8#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:1-8#2/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:1-8#2/r1.claim: Jahr is speaking aloud, while isrār is its opposite; sirr is speech kept within oneself, and akhfā is a superlative meaning more hidden, not a past-tense verb with Allah as subject. Its indefinite form intensifies concealment.
TABATABAI:20:1-8#2/r1.anchor: أفعل التفضيل من الخفاء على ما يعطيه سياق الترقي في الآية

TABATABAI:20:1-8#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:1-8#2/r2.speaker: بعضهم
TABATABAI:20:1-8#2/r2.claim: He rejects the view that akhfā is a past-tense verb meaning Allah knows the secret and what He has hidden.
TABATABAI:20:1-8#2/r2.anchor: ولا يصغى إلى قول من قال إن { أخفى } فعل ماض فاعله

TABATABAI:20:1-8#2/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:1-8#2/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:1-8#2/r3.claim: Moving from audible speech to the inner secret and then what is still more hidden proves Allah knows everything, even an intention concealed from its own thinker.
TABATABAI:20:1-8#2/r3.anchor: وذكر الجهر بالقول في الآية أولا ثم إثبات العلم بما هو أدق منه وهو السر والترقي إلى أخفى يدل على أن المراد إثبات العلم بالجميع

TABATABAI:20:1-8#2/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:1-8#2/r4.speaker: بعضهم
TABATABAI:20:1-8#2/r4.claim: Another interpretation takes sirr as speech whispered to someone else and akhfā as a thought in the mind; the author accepts the account of whispering but says speech is secret only when kept within oneself.
TABATABAI:20:1-8#2/r4.anchor: وذكر بعضهم أن المراد بالسر ما أسررته من القول إلى غيرك ولم ترفع صوتك به

TABATABAI:20:1-8#2/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:1-8#2/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:1-8#2/r5.claim: The verse’s compact structure states Allah knows the secret and what is more hidden, which also answers whether He knows what is spoken aloud: if He knows the more hidden, He certainly knows the audible.
TABATABAI:20:1-8#2/r5.anchor: فدل على الجواب في شقي الترديد معا وعلى معنى الأولوية بأوجز بيان

TABATABAI:20:1-8#2/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:1-8#2/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:1-8#2/r6.claim: The verse establishes Allah’s knowledge of everything visible and hidden, paralleling the statement that He knows what enters and leaves the earth after settling over the Throne.
TABATABAI:20:1-8#2/r6.anchor: فالآية تثبت علمه تعالى بكل شيء ظاهر أو خفي فهي في ذكر العلم عقيب الاستواء على العرش نظيرة قوله تعالى

TABATABAI:20:8#3/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:8#3/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:8#3/r1.claim: Knowledge of events within Allah’s kingdom entails His approval and permission; from another angle it reflects His will for the existing order, which is governance. Verse 20:7 thus establishes universal management, while 20:6 establishes universal ownership; together they prove absolute lordship.
TABATABAI:20:8#3/r1.anchor: فالآية تثبت عموم التدبير كما أن الآية السابقة كانت تثبت عموم الملك ومجموع مدلوليهما هو الملك والتدبير

TABATABAI:20:1-8#10/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:1-8#10/r4.speaker: أبو عبد الله عن محمد بن مسلم
TABATABAI:20:1-8#10/r4.claim: Abu Abd Allah explains the secret as what one conceals within oneself, and what is more hidden as a thought that crosses one's mind and is then forgotten.
TABATABAI:20:1-8#10/r4.anchor: عن محد بن مسلم قال سألت أبا عبد الله عليه السلام عن قول الله عز وجل { يعلم السر وأخفى } قال السر ما أكننته في نفسك

TABATABAI:20:1-8#10/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:1-8#10/r5.speaker: السيدان الباقر والصادق
TABATABAI:20:1-8#10/r5.claim: Al-Majmaʿ attributes the same explanation to al-Baqir and al-Sadiq: the secret is concealed within oneself; the more hidden is a thought later forgotten.
TABATABAI:20:1-8#10/r5.anchor: روي عن السيدين الباقر والصادق عليهما السلام { السر } ما أخفيته في نفسك و { أخفى } ما خطر ببالك ثم أنسيته

ZAJJAJ:v3p350/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p350/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p350/r5.claim: The secret is what one conceals within oneself; what is more hidden is the unseen known only to God.
ZAJJAJ:v3p350/r5.anchor: فالسر ما أكننته في نفسك، و " أخفى " ما يكون من الغيب

TABRISI:20:2-8/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:2-8/r14.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:2-8/r14.claim: The warning not to raise one's voice means there is no need to strain: God knows what is secret and what is even more hidden.
TABRISI:20:2-8/r14.anchor: فلا تجهد نفسك برفع الصوت فإنك وإن لم تجهر

TABRISI:20:2-8/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:2-8/r15.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:2-8/r15.claim: The comparative phrase omits “than it” because the comparison is understood, as in saying someone is like an elephant or bigger.
TABRISI:20:2-8/r15.anchor: ولم يقل وأخفى منه لدلالة الكلام عليه كما يقول القائل

TABRISI:20:2-8/r16.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:2-8/r16.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:20:2-8/r16.claim: An alternative paraphrase says that whether one speaks aloud or not, God knows the secret and what is more hidden than it.
TABRISI:20:2-8/r16.anchor: أو لا تجهر فإنه يعلم السر وأخفى منه

TABRISI:20:2-8/r17.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:2-8/r17.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:20:2-8/r17.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the secret is what a person privately tells someone else, while the more hidden is what the person keeps inside without telling anyone.

TABRISI:20:2-8/r18.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:2-8/r18.speaker: قتادة وسعيد بن جبير وابن زيد
TABRISI:20:2-8/r18.claim: Qatādah, Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, and Ibn Zayd say the secret is what a servant hides within, and the more hidden is what has not yet existed or been concealed by anyone.
TABRISI:20:2-8/r18.anchor: عن قتادة وسعيد بن جبير وابن زيد

TABRISI:20:2-8/r19.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:2-8/r19.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:20:2-8/r19.claim: Another explanation calls the secret what one says inwardly and the more hidden what one will later intend to say to oneself.
TABRISI:20:2-8/r19.anchor: السر ما تحدث به نفسك وأخفى منه ما تريد

TABRISI:20:2-8/r20.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:2-8/r20.speaker: مجاهد
TABRISI:20:2-8/r20.claim: Mujāhid interprets the secret as deeds hidden from people and the more hidden as inner whispering.
TABRISI:20:2-8/r20.anchor: العمل الذي تستره عن الناس وأخفى منه الوسوسة عن مجاهد

TABRISI:20:2-8/r21.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:2-8/r21.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
TABRISI:20:2-8/r21.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam takes the secret as the creatures' secrets and reads akhfā as a past-tense verb, God having concealed His own secret.
TABRISI:20:2-8/r21.anchor: وأخفى أي سر نفسه عن زيد بن أسلم

TABRISI:20:2-8/r22.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:2-8/r22.speaker: الباقر والصادق
TABRISI:20:2-8/r22.claim: Al-Bāqir and al-Ṣādiq say the secret is what one conceals within oneself and akhfā is what comes to mind and is then forgotten.

THALABI:v6p238/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p238/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v6p238/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses the most hidden thing as a person's own inner conversation.
THALABI:v6p238/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله يعلم السر وأخفى قال: وأخفى حديث نفسك نفسك.

THALABI:v6p238/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p238/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v6p238/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas, through al-Dahhak, says the secret is what one conceals in oneself and the more hidden is what one will later tell oneself, even without knowing it now.
THALABI:v6p238/r7.anchor: عن الضحاك عن ابن عباس قال: السر ما أسررت في نفسك، وأخفى أخفى من السر، ما ستحدث به نفسك

THALABI:v6p238/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p238/r8.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
THALABI:v6p238/r8.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr says the secret is today's concealed thought and the more hidden is a future thought not yet formed; God knows both today and tomorrow's thoughts.
THALABI:v6p238/r8.anchor: وروى عطاء بن السائب عن سعيد بن جبير قال: السر ما تسر في نفسك، وأخفى من السر ما لم يكن وهو كائن

THALABI:v6p238/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p238/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v6p238/r9.claim: Ibn Abbas says the secret is what a person hides now and the more hidden is a future deed unknown even to its doer; God's knowledge of past and future is one, and all creatures are alike to Him.
THALABI:v6p238/r9.anchor: وروى علي بن أبي طلحة عن ابن عباس قال: السر ما أسر ابن آدم في نفسه، وأخفى ما خفي على ابن آدم مما هو فاعله قبل أن يعلمه

THALABI:v6p238#2/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p238#2/r1.speaker: مجاهد
THALABI:v6p238#2/r1.claim: Mujahid says the secret is a deed hidden from people and the more hidden is inner whispering.
THALABI:v6p238#2/r1.anchor: وقال مجاهد: السر العمل الذي يسرون من الناس، وأخفى الوسوسة

THALABI:v6p238#2/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p238#2/r2.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
THALABI:v6p238#2/r2.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam says God knows the servants' secrets but keeps His own secret beyond their knowledge.
THALABI:v6p238#2/r2.anchor: وقال زيد بن أسلم: معناه يعلم أسرار العباد، وأخفى سره فلا يعلم.

THALABI:v6p238#2/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p238#2/r3.speaker: الحسن
THALABI:v6p238#2/r3.claim: Al-Hasan says a secret is what a person confides to someone else, while the more hidden is what he keeps within himself.
THALABI:v6p238#2/r3.anchor: وقال الحسن: السر ما أسر الرجل إلى غيره، وأخفى من ذلك ما أسره في نفسه.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p253/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p253/r3.speaker: قتادة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p253/r3.claim: Qatada says the secret is what one tells oneself, while the more hidden is what will happen before one has even thought it.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p253/r3.anchor: سعيد، عن قتادة قال: السر ما حدثت به نفسك، وأخفى منه ما هو كائن مما لم تحدث به نفسك.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p253/r4.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p253/r4.speaker: قتادة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p253/r4.claim: In another explanation, Qatada says the secret is what one conceals inside, and the more hidden is what God knows one will do.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p253/r4.anchor: الحسن بن دينار، عن قتادة قال: السر ما أخفيت في نفسك، وأخفى منه ما علم الله تبارك وتعالى أنك عامل.

SAMIN-DURR:20:7/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:7/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:7/r1.claim: أخفى may be the comparative adjective “more hidden than the secret.”
SAMIN-DURR:20:7/r1.anchor: جوزوا فيه وجهين، أحدهما: أنه أفعل تفضيل، أي: وأخفى من السر

SAMIN-DURR:20:7/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:7/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:7/r2.claim: Alternatively, أخفى is a past verb: God concealed the unseen from His servants, as echoed in 20:110.
SAMIN-DURR:20:7/r2.anchor: والثاني: أنه فعل ماض أي: وأخفى الله عن عباده غيبه كقوله: ولا يحيطون به علما

ASAD-NOTES:20:6/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:20:6/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:20:6/r2.claim: God knows even what is hidden within people, whether they speak aloud or not.
ASAD-NOTES:20:6/r2.anchor: if thou say anything aloud, [He hears it - ] since, behold, He knows [even] the secret [thoughts of man] as well as all that is yet more hidden

ASAD-NOTES:20:6#n4/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:20:6#n4/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:20:6#n4/r1.claim: God knows both unspoken conscious thoughts and what takes place in the subconscious.
ASAD-NOTES:20:6#n4/r1.anchor: He knows not only man's unspoken, conscious thoughts but also all that goes on within his subconscious self

NASHR:v2p233/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p233/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p233/r1.claim: At connection, when the following tāʾ follows a madd or layn letter, its length is retained; with other preceding sukūn, including tanwīn, the sounds may be joined when Arabic usage permits and transmission supports it.
NASHR:v2p233/r1.anchor: فإن كان قبلها حرف مد ولين. نحو ولا تيمموا، وعنه تلهى أثبته ومد لالتقاء الساكنين

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p15#2/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p15#2/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p15#2/r1.claim: Qatada says God knows both what a person has told himself and what he has not yet thought about, which is still to come.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p15#2/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله ﴿ السر وأخفى ﴾ من السر ما حدثت به نفسك وما لم تحدث به نفسك أيضا مما هو كائن

ALUSI-FULL:v16p162/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p162/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p162/r1.claim: This verse follows the statement of God's power over all beings by explaining the comprehensiveness of His knowledge.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p162/r1.anchor: لاحاطة علمه تعالى بجميع الأشياء اثر بيان شمول قدرته تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v16p162/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p162/r2.speaker: البحر
ALUSI-FULL:v16p162/r2.claim: Al-Bahr says the address is to the Prophet, with his community intended; Alusi also allows it to address humanity generally.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p162/r2.anchor: للنبى ( صلى الله عليه وسلم ) والمراد امته عليه الصلاة والسلام وجوز أن يكون عاما

ALUSI-FULL:v16p162/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p162/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p162/r3.claim: Tajhar means to raise one's voice in speech.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p162/r3.anchor: وان ترفع صوتك ايها الانسان بالقول

ALUSI-FULL:v16p162/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p162/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p162/r4.claim: The secret is what one confides to another without raising one's voice.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p162/r4.anchor: أي ما اسررته إلى غيرك ولم ترفع صوتك به

ALUSI-FULL:v16p162/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p162/r5.speaker: الحسن، عكرمة
ALUSI-FULL:v16p162/r5.claim: Al-Hasan and Ikrimah explain akhfa as something even more hidden: a thought that crosses one's mind without being spoken.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p162/r5.anchor: وهو ما اخطرته ببالك من غير أن تتفوه به اصلا وروى ذلك عن الحسن وعكرمه

ALUSI-FULL:v16p162/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p162/r6.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
ALUSI-FULL:v16p162/r6.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr explains the secret as what is concealed within oneself and akhfa as what one will conceal there later.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p162/r6.anchor: أو ما ايررته في نفسك وما ستسره فيها وروى ذلك عن سعيد بن جبير

ALUSI-FULL:v16p162/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p162/r7.speaker: الباقر والصادق
ALUSI-FULL:v16p162/r7.claim: Al-Baqir and al-Sadiq say the secret is what one hides within, while akhfa is a thought that occurs and is then forgotten.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p162/r7.anchor: وروى عن السيدين الباقر والصادق السر ما اخفيته في نفسك والاخفى ما خطر ببالك ثم انسيته

ALUSI-FULL:v16p162/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p162/r8.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
ALUSI-FULL:v16p162/r8.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam reportedly reads akhfa as a past verb coordinated with yaʿlam: God knows people's secrets and what He has hidden from them; Abu al-Shaykh transmits it in al-Azama.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p162/r8.anchor: وروى ذلك أبو الشيخ في العظمه عن زيد بن اسلم وهو خلاف الظاهر جدا

ALUSI-FULL:v16p162/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p162/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p162/r9.claim: Alusi calls the past-verb reading far from the apparent sense and prefers akhfa as a comparative or superlative, with indefinite form for intensity.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p162/r9.anchor: وهو خلاف الظاهر جدا فالمعول عليه أنه افعل تفضيل والتنكير للمبالغة في الخفاء

ALUSI-FULL:v16p162/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p162/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p162/r10.claim: Some take al-qawl broadly to include God's remembrance and other speech; a group restricts it to remembrance and supplication addressed to God, with the definite article referring to that context.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p162/r10.anchor: والمتبادر من القول ما يشمل ذكر الله تعالى وغيره واليه ذهب بعضه وخصه جماعة بذكره سبحانه ودعائه

ALUSI-FULL:v16p162/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p162/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p162/r11.claim: The conditional clause stands in place of an answer, although God's knowledge is not actually contingent on whether or when anyone speaks aloud.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p162/r11.anchor: الخ قائم مقام جواب الشرط وليس الجواب في الحقيقة لأن علمه تعالى السر واخفى ثابت قبل الجهر بالقول وبعده

ALUSI-FULL:v16p162/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p162/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p162/r12.claim: One implied expansion is: if you speak aloud, know that God knows it, along with the secret and the more hidden.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p162/r12.anchor: والأصل عند البعض وان يجهر بالقول فاعلم أن الله تعالى يعلمه فانه يعلم السر واخفى

ALUSI-FULL:v16p162/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p162/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p162/r13.claim: Another implied expansion is that God has no need of one's audible address because He already knows the secret and the more hidden.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p162/r13.anchor: فاعلم أن الله سبحانه غنى عن جهرك فانه الخ

ALUSI-FULL:v16p162/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p162/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p162/r14.claim: One explanation urges care in public speech: knowing God hears one's aloud words deters speaking evil; public speech is singled out because most conversation is aloud.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p162/r14.anchor: وهذا على ما قيل إرشاد للعباد إلى التحري والاحتياط حين الجهر فان من علم أن الله تعالى يعلم جهره

ALUSI-FULL:v16p162/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p162/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p162/r15.claim: Another explanation says audible remembrance and supplication serve to shape and reinforce one's own recollection, prevent distraction, and cut off intrusive thoughts, not to inform God.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p162/r15.anchor: إرشاد للعباد إلى أن الجهر بذكر الله تعالى ودعائه ليس لاسماعه سبحانه بل لغرض أخر من تصوير النفس بالذكر

ALUSI-FULL:v16p162/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p162/r16.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p162/r16.claim: Some infer a prohibition on aloud dhikr and supplication from the verse about remembering inwardly; Alusi says a blanket prohibition should not be asserted.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p162/r16.anchor: لا ينبغى أن يكون على اطلاقه

ALUSI-FULL:v16p162#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p162#2/r1.speaker: النووي
ALUSI-FULL:v16p162#2/r1.claim: Al-Nawawi says aloud dhikr is recommended when no religious harm is present, and preferable to silent dhikr in the Shafi'i school; it is also an apparent Hanbali position and one Maliki narration.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p162#2/r1.anchor: الذي نص عليه الأمام النووى في فتاويه أن الجهر بالذكر حيث لا محذور شرعيا مشروع مندوب اليه بل هو افضل من الأخفاء في مذهب الأمام الشافعى

ALUSI-FULL:v16p162#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p162#2/r2.speaker: قاضيخان
ALUSI-FULL:v16p162#2/r2.claim: Qadi Khan's dislike of raising the voice in dhikr concerns those accompanying a funeral, matching the Shafi'i position, rather than dhikr generally.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p162#2/r2.anchor: ويكره رفع الصوت بالذكر فالظاهر أنه لمن يمشي مع الجنازة كما هو مذهب الشافعية لا مطلقا

ALUSI-FULL:v16p162#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p162#2/r3.speaker: أبو يوسف ومحمد وأبو حنيفة
ALUSI-FULL:v16p162#2/r3.claim: The two companions approve aloud takbir on Eid al-Fitr as on al-Adha; a narration from Abu Hanifa and the apparent evidence of his Musnad also support general aloud dhikr.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p162#2/r3.anchor: وهو قول الأمامين في تكبير عيد الفطر كالاضحى ورواية عن الأمام أبى حنيفة نفسه

ALUSI-FULL:v16p162#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p162#2/r4.speaker: أبو حنيفة
ALUSI-FULL:v16p162#2/r4.claim: As quoted by Ibn al-Humam, Abu Hanifa calls raising the voice in dhikr an innovation contrary to the command to remember inwardly, except where revelation prescribes aloud remembrance at Eid al-Adha.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p162#2/r4.anchor: قال أبو حنيفه : رفع الصوت بالذكر بدعة

ALUSI-FULL:v16p162#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p162#2/r5.speaker: السيوطي
ALUSI-FULL:v16p162#2/r5.claim: Al-Suyuti's first answer to the prohibition argument is that the inward-remembrance verse is Meccan and its restriction fell away after the Hijra.

ALUSI-FULL:v16p162#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p162#2/r6.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن أسلم وابن جرير
ALUSI-FULL:v16p162#2/r6.claim: Al-Suyuti's second answer, shared by Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam and Ibn Jarir, applies the inward-remembrance verse to dhikr during Quran recitation, supported by its following context.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p162#2/r6.anchor: منهم عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن اسلم وابن جرير حملوا الآية

ALUSI-FULL:v16p162#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p162#2/r7.speaker: بعض الصوفية
ALUSI-FULL:v16p162#2/r7.claim: Al-Suyuti's third answer, attributed to some Sufis, limits the command to the Prophet, while others troubled by whispering should use aloud remembrance; Alusi finds this questionable.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p162#2/r7.anchor: الثالث ما ذكره بعض الصوفية أن الأمر في الآية خاص بالنبى ( صلى الله عليه وسلم ) الكامل المكمل

ALUSI-FULL:v16p162#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p162#2/r8.speaker: بعض المحققين
ALUSI-FULL:v16p162#2/r8.claim: Some verifiers prefer interpreting the instruction as against excessive or unnecessary loudness, leaving moderate speech and the volume needed for a purpose permitted.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p162#2/r8.anchor: واختار بعض المحققين أن المراد دون الجهر البالغ أو الزائد على قدر الحاجة

ALUSI-FULL:v16p162#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p162#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p162#2/r9.claim: Alusi says more than twenty sound reports establish that the Prophet often voiced dhikr aloud.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p162#2/r9.anchor: حديثا في أنه ( صلى الله عليه وسلم ) كثيرا ما كان يجهر بالذكر

ALUSI-FULL:v16p162#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p162#2/r10.speaker: عبد الله بن الزبير
ALUSI-FULL:v16p162#2/r10.claim: Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr reports that after prayer the Prophet said a lengthy formula of remembrance in a loud voice; Alusi explains this as serving teaching or a similar need.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p162#2/r10.anchor: وصح عن أبى الزبير أنه سمع عبد الله ابن الزبير يقول

ALUSI-FULL:v16p162#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p162#2/r11.speaker: أبو موسى الأشعري
ALUSI-FULL:v16p162#2/r11.claim: In a report in both Sahih collections, Abu Musa says the companions raised voices at a valley; the Prophet told them to be gentle because God is near, hearing, and present.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p162#2/r11.anchor: في الصحيحين من حديث أبى موسى الأشعرى قال

ALUSI-FULL:v16p162#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p162#2/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p162#2/r12.claim: The Prophet's command arbiʿu means to be gentle and not strain yourselves; its implied prohibition targets excessive volume, not all audible dhikr.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p162#2/r12.anchor: محمول على أن النهى المستفاد التزاما من أمر اربعوا الذي بمعنى ارفقوا ولا تجهدوا أنفسكم مراد به النهى عن المبالغة في رفع الصوت

ALUSI-FULL:v16p162#2/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p162#2/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p162#2/r13.claim: Distinguishing degrees of loudness reconciles the conflicting reports from Abu Hanifa about voiced remembrance.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p162#2/r13.anchor: وبتقسيم الجهر واختلاف اقسامه في الحكم يجمع بين الروايتين المختلفتين عن الأمام أبى حنيفة

ALUSI-FULL:v16p162#2/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p162#2/r14.speaker: ابن مسعود
ALUSI-FULL:v16p162#2/r14.claim: The report that Ibn Masud removed people from a mosque for loud group dhikr is not sound according to hadith authorities; if sound, it concerns excessive volume or is outweighed by evidence for aloud dhikr.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p162#2/r14.anchor: ذكر في الواقعات عن ابن مسعود من أنه رأى قوما يهللون برفع الصوت في المسجد

ALUSI-FULL:v16p162#2/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p162#2/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p162#2/r15.claim: Alusi calls the hadith saying the best remembrance is hidden sound, and limits its application to settings where ostentation or self-admiration is feared.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p162#2/r15.anchor: وخبر خير الذكر الخفى وخير الرزق أو العيش ما يكفي صحيح

ALUSI-FULL:v16p163/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p163/r1.speaker: السيوطي
ALUSI-FULL:v16p163/r1.claim: Al-Suyuti attributes the sound hidden-remembrance hadith to Ahmad, Ibn Hibban, and al-Bayhaqi, reporting from Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas; Abu al-Fath also cites Abu Awana's Sahih.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p163/r1.anchor: وعزاه الأمام السيوطي إلى الأمام أحمد وابن حيان والبيهقي عن سعد ابن أبى وقاص

ALUSI-FULL:v16p163/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p163/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p163/r2.claim: The preference for hidden remembrance applies to someone in a place where ostentation, self-admiration, or similar motives are feared.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p163/r2.anchor: وهو محمول على من كان في موضع يخاف فيه الرياء أو الأعجاب أو نحوهما

ALUSI-FULL:v16p163/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p163/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p163/r3.claim: Authentic reports also establish that the Prophet voiced supplication and sermons, although several eminent scholars say silent supplication is preferable.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p163/r3.anchor: جهر بالدعاء وبالمواعض لكن قال غير واحد من الأجلة

ALUSI-FULL:v16p163/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p163/r4.speaker: ابن حجر الهيتمي
ALUSI-FULL:v16p163/r4.claim: Ibn Hajar al-Haytami defines aloud remembrance as loud enough for another person to hear, and inward remembrance as audible to oneself.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p163/r4.anchor: وحد بالجهر على ما ذكره ابن حجر الهيتمى في المنهج القويم أن يكون بحيث يسمع غيره والأسرار بحيث يسمع نفسه

ALUSI-FULL:v16p163/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p163/r5.speaker: رواية عن الحنفية
ALUSI-FULL:v16p163/r5.claim: One Hanafi narration sets the minimum aloud recitation at hearing oneself and the minimum quiet recitation at merely articulating letters; al-Karkhi holds this view.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p163/r5.anchor: وعند الحنفيه في رواية ادنى الجهر اسماع نفسه وادنى المخافتة تصحيح الحروف وهو قول الكرخى

ALUSI-FULL:v16p163/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p163/r6.speaker: الشيخان الهندواني والفضلي
ALUSI-FULL:v16p163/r6.claim: The sounder position in al-Muhit, held by most, requires aloud recitation to be heard by another and quiet recitation to be heard by oneself.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p163/r6.anchor: والأصح كما في المحيط قول الشيخين الهندوانى والفضلى هو الذي عليه الأكثر أن أدنى الجهر اسماع غيره وأدنى المخافتة إسماع نفسه

ALUSI-FULL:v16p163/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p163/r7.speaker: ابن الهمام
ALUSI-FULL:v16p163/r7.claim: Ibn al-Humam argues that articulation without sound produces no letters, speech, reading, or quiet recitation, since letters are qualities of sound.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p163/r7.anchor: إن تصحيح الحروف بلا صوت إيماء إلى الحروف بعضلات المخارج لا حروف إذ الحروف كيفية تعرض للصوت

ALUSI-FULL:v16p163/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p163/r8.speaker: إبراهيم الكوراني
ALUSI-FULL:v16p163/r8.claim: Ibrahim al-Kurani wrote two treatises defending aloud dhikr against a ninth-century Hanafi notable who had categorically branded it forbidden innovation and written against it.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p163/r8.anchor: وقد ألف الشيخ إبراهيم الكورانى عليه الرحمة في تحقيق هذه المسألة رسالتين جليلتين سمى اولاهما نشر الزهر في الذكر بالجهر

ALUSI-FULL:v16p209#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p209#2/r5.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v16p209#2/r5.claim: One explanation calls the secret something latent in the heart like fire in damp wood, stirred into view by will; the more hidden thing lies within it.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p209#2/r5.anchor: قيل : السر أمر كامن فى القلب كمون النار فى الشجر الرطب حيث تثيره الأرادة لا يطلع عليه الملك

ALUSI-FULL:v16p209#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p209#2/r6.speaker: بعض الصوفية
ALUSI-FULL:v16p209#2/r6.claim: Some Sufis define the secret as a subtle center between heart and spirit, the seat of spiritual mysteries, and the hidden as between spirit and divine presence, where divine lights descend.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p209#2/r6.anchor: وعند بعض الصوفية السر لطيفه بين القلب والروح وهو معدن الأسرار الروحانية والخفى لطيفة بين الروح والحضرة الالهية

ALUSI-FULL:v16p209#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p209#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p209#2/r7.claim: Although some infer that loud remembrance is not prescribed, al-Alūsī says it is prescribed with its conditions; absent a text preferring volume or concealment, the better mode varies by person, circumstance, and time.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p209#2/r7.anchor: وقد استدل بعض الناس بهذه الآية على عدم مشروعية الجهر بالذكر والحق أنه مشروع بشرطه

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:7/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:7/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:7/r1.claim: Even if one raises one’s voice in remembrance or invocation, God knows the secret and what is more hidden, the self’s inward thought; He does not need loud speech.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:7/r1.anchor: أي وإن تجهر بذكر الله ودعائه فاعلم أنه غني عن جهرك فإنه سبحانه يعلم السر وأخفى منه، وهو ضمير النفس.

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:7/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:7/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:7/r2.claim: Public remembrance shapes it in the self, prevents distraction, and humbles the worshipper; it is not to inform God.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:7/r2.anchor: وفيه تنبيه على أن شرع الذكر والدعاء والجهر فيما ليس لإعلام الله بل لتصوير النفس بالذكر ورسوخه فيها ومنعها عن الاشتغال بغيره

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:7/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:7/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:7/r3.claim: The passage moves from God’s complete attributes to affirm that He alone possesses their implications.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:7/r3.anchor: ثم إنه لما ظهر بذلك أنه المستجمع لصفات الألوهية بين أنه المتفرد بها

DURR-FULL:v5p552/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p552/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p552/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says the secret is what a person hides within, while the more hidden is what he will do before knowing it; God knows past and future equally, and all creatures are as one person to Him, as in 31:28.
DURR-FULL:v5p552/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله: {يعلم السر وأخفى} قال: السر ما أسره ابن آدم في نفسه

DURR-FULL:v5p552/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p552/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p552/r3.claim: A report authenticated by al-Hakim says the secret is what you know, while the more hidden is what God casts into your heart before you know it.
DURR-FULL:v5p552/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله: {يعلم السر وأخفى} قال: السر ما علمته أنت وأخفى ما قذف الله في قلبك

DURR-FULL:v5p552/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p552/r4.speaker: author
DURR-FULL:v5p552/r4.claim: A report cited from the works of Abd Allah ibn Ahmad, Abu al-Shaykh, and al-Bayhaqi says God knows what one conceals within and what one will do tomorrow.
DURR-FULL:v5p552/r4.anchor: بلفظ: يعلم ما تسر في نفسك ويعلم ما تعمل غدا

DURR-FULL:v5p552/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p552/r5.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v5p552/r5.claim: Qatada says the more hidden than private speech is both what a person tells himself and what he has not yet told himself but will happen.
DURR-FULL:v5p552/r5.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله: {يعلم السر وأخفى} قال: أخفى من السر ما حدثت به نفسك

DURR-FULL:v5p552/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p552/r6.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v5p552/r6.claim: Mujahid identifies the hidden as inner whispering and the secret as deeds concealed from other people.
DURR-FULL:v5p552/r6.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله: {يعلم السر وأخفى} قال: الوسوسة والسر العمل الذي تسرون من الناس

DURR-FULL:v5p552/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p552/r7.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v5p552/r7.claim: Al-Hasan says the secret is what a man confides to another, and what is more hidden is what he conceals within himself.
DURR-FULL:v5p552/r7.anchor: عن الحسن قال: السر ما أسر الرجل إلى غيره وأخفى من ذلك ما أسر في نفسه

DURR-FULL:v5p553/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p553/r1.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
DURR-FULL:v5p553/r1.claim: Sa‘id ibn Jubayr says the secret is what a person keeps within himself, and the more hidden is what has not yet occurred but will occur.
DURR-FULL:v5p553/r1.anchor: قال: السر ما تسر في نفسك وأخفى من السر ما لم يكن بعد

DURR-FULL:v5p553/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p553/r2.speaker: عكرمة
DURR-FULL:v5p553/r2.claim: Ikrima says the secret is what a man tells his family, and the more hidden is what he says inwardly.
DURR-FULL:v5p553/r2.anchor: عن عكرمة في الآية قال: السر ما حدث به الرجل أهله

DURR-FULL:v5p553/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p553/r3.speaker: الضحاك
DURR-FULL:v5p553/r3.claim: Al-Dahhak says the secret is what one hides within oneself, while the more hidden is what one has not thought yet.
DURR-FULL:v5p553/r3.anchor: عن الضحاك في قوله: {يعلم السر وأخفى} قال: السر ما أسررت في نفسك

DURR-FULL:v5p553/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p553/r4.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
DURR-FULL:v5p553/r4.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam says God knows the servants’ secrets, but His own secret remains unknown to them.
DURR-FULL:v5p553/r4.anchor: عن زيد بن أسلم في قوله: {يعلم السر وأخفى} قال: يعلم أسرار العباد

BURSEVI:v5p281#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p281#2/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p281#2/r8.claim: To make the saying aloud is to announce God’s remembrance and invocation; the following explanation is continued in the next segment.

BURSEVI:v5p282/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p282/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p282/r1.claim: God is independent of public remembrance and invocation, since He knows both the secret and what is more hidden.
BURSEVI:v5p282/r1.anchor: فاعلم أنه تعالى غني عن جهرك وإعلانك

BURSEVI:v5p282/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p282/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p282/r2.claim: The present tense denotes continuous knowledge in every age; divine knowledge transcends time and place, and change belongs to its objects, not to knowledge itself.
BURSEVI:v5p282/r2.anchor: علمهما منه مستمر دائم وذلك أن علمه تعالى منزه عن الزمان كما هو منزه عن المكان

BURSEVI:v5p282/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p282/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p282/r3.claim: Sirr is what one conceals; the indefinite akhfā intensifies hiddenness and can mean a thought kept from others, an unspoken thought, or a thought one will later form without anticipating it.
BURSEVI:v5p282/r3.anchor: والسر واحد الأسرار وهو ما يكتم ومنه أسر الحديث إذا أخفاه وتنكير أخفى للمبالغة في الخفاء

BURSEVI:v5p282/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p282/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p282/r4.claim: The wording may prohibit loudness, as in 7:205, or guide worshippers that audible dhikr serves inner imprint, focus, resistance to distraction, humility, awakening others, and spreading blessings and witnesses.
BURSEVI:v5p282/r4.anchor: وهذا إما نهي عن الجهر كقوله تعالى : {واذكر ربك في نفسك

BURSEVI:v5p282/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p282/r5.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
BURSEVI:v5p282/r5.claim: At Khaybar, after people raised their voices with takbīr and tahlīl from a valley, the Prophet told them to be gentle because they call One who hears and is near, not a deaf or absent being.
BURSEVI:v5p282/r5.anchor: وجاء أنه عليه السلام لما توجه إلى خيبر أشرف الناس على واد فرفعوا أصواتهم بالتكبير

BURSEVI:v5p282/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p282/r6.speaker: إنسان العيون
BURSEVI:v5p282/r6.claim: The prohibition is reconciled with the Prophet’s command to raise voices in talbiya by limiting it to excessive loudness beyond ordinary levels that can cause harm.
BURSEVI:v5p282/r6.anchor: المنهى عنه هنا الرفع الخارج عن العادة الذي ربما آذى بدليل قوله عليه السلام أربعوا على أنفسكم

BURSEVI:v5p282/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p282/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p282/r7.claim: The Prophet also restrained loudness to hide plans from enemies and suit spiritually realized companions’ preference for moderation; Sufis use audible dhikr to intimidate the ego and Satan and drive away whispering, with louder voices for necessity.
BURSEVI:v5p282/r7.anchor: ولذا اعتاد الصوفية بجهر الذكر تهييبا لهما وطردا للوسوسة

BURSEVI:v5p282/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p282/r8.speaker: الحكماء
BURSEVI:v5p282/r8.claim: The philosophers recommend that rulers speak loudly so listeners feel awe and the words make a stronger impression.
BURSEVI:v5p282/r8.anchor: وقد اختار الحكماء للسلطان جهارة الصوت في كلامه ليكون أهيب لسامعيه وأوقع في قلوبهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p188/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p188/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p188/r1.claim: This sentence follows the statement of God’s dominion in 20:6, adding the breadth of His knowledge; it precedes 20:8, while its original order would place the conditional clause after the assertion.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p188/r1.anchor: عطف على جملة { له ما في السموات وما في الأرض } ( طه : 6 ) لدلالة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p188/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p188/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p188/r2.claim: The conditional phrase is parenthetical between “He knows the secret and what is more hidden” and “God—there is no deity but Him”; presenting the assertion as proof of its actuality is madhhab kalāmī.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p188/r2.anchor: وأصل النظم : ويعلم السر وأخفى إن تجهر بالقول ؛ فموقع قوله : { وإن تجهر بالقول }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p188/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p188/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p188/r3.claim: God knows the secret and what is still more hidden even when someone speaks aloud to be heard; loudness adds nothing because He already knows the secret.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p188/r3.anchor: والمعنى : إنه يعلم السر وأخفى من السر في الأحوال

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p188/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p188/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p188/r4.claim: A conditional form can assert what holds in every case rather than make the result contingent; the cited examples use it to express universality.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p188/r4.anchor: وذلك في كل شرط لا يقصد به التعليق بل يقصد التحقيق

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p188/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p188/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p188/r5.claim: Abū Kabīr’s “when the anxious one sleeps” illustrates a condition meaning that the subject stays wakeful whenever others sleep.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p188/r5.anchor: سهدا إذا ما نام ليل الهوجل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p188/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p188/r6.speaker: بشامة بن حزن النهشلي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p188/r6.claim: Bashāma’s conditional about warriors drawing back exemplifies a condition used to assert what happens whenever the circumstance occurs.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p188/r6.anchor:
وقول بشامة بن حزن النهشلي :
إذا الكماة تنحوا أن يصيبهم
حد الظبات وصلناها بأيدينا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p188/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p188/r7.speaker: إبراهيم بن كنيف النبهاني
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p188/r7.claim: Ibrāhīm’s conditional about the days’ reversals presents steadfastness as holding through every turn of fortune.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p188/r7.anchor:
وقول إبراهيم بن كنيف النبهاني :
فإن تكن الأيام جالت صروفها
ببؤسى ونعمى والحوادث تفعل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p188/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p188/r8.speaker: القطامي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p188/r8.claim: Al-Quṭāmī’s question about whether civilization impresses someone is another conditional used rhetorically to generalize.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p188/r8.anchor:
وقول القطامي :
فمن تكن الحضارة أعجبته
فأي رجال بادية ترانا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p188/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p188/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p188/r9.claim: The address may be to the Prophet, with others included, or to no particular person, in which case it addresses everyone.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p188/r9.anchor: فالخطاب في قوله وإن تجهر } يجوز أن يكون خطابا للنبيء صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p188/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p188/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p188/r10.claim: The verse singles out what is heard because secret speech is ordinarily among the hardest things for people to know.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p188/r10.anchor: واختير في إثبات سعة علم الله تعالى خصوص علمه بالمسموعات لأن السر أخفى الأشياء عن علم الناس

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p188/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p188/r11.speaker: عبدالله بن مسعود
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p188/r11.claim: Al-Bukhārī reports from Ibn Masʿūd that three men near the Kaʿba debated whether God hears quiet speech; one concluded that if He hears them aloud, He also hears them secretly.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p188/r11.anchor: وفي ( صحيح البخاري ) عن عبدالله بن مسعود قال : اجتمع عند البيت ثقفيان وقرشي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p188/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p188/r12.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p188/r12.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr thinks this verse alludes to the same dispute recalled in 41:22, and links it to God knowing what people conceal beneath their clothes.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p188/r12.anchor: ولا أحسب هذه الآية إلا ناظرة إلى مثل ما نظرت الآية الآنفة الذكر .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p190/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p190/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p190/r1.claim: Although secret speech might seem more apt to demonstrate divine omniscience, the choice to posit loud speech suits this context and the Ibn Masʿūd report.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p190/r1.anchor: يبقى النظر في توجيه الإتيان بهذا الشرط بطريقة الاعتراض ، وتوجيه اختيار فرض الشرط بحالة الجهر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p190/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p190/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p190/r2.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr proposes that the condition concerns the Prophet’s effort to recite aloud; as with 7:205, it may have been superseded by 15:94, teaching equal divine knowledge of open and quiet supplication and rejecting the polytheists’ assumption.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p190/r2.anchor: وأحسب لفرض الشرط بحالة الجهر بالقول خصوصية بهذا السياق اقتضاها اجتهاد النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p190/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p190/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p190/r3.claim: Qawl is a verbal noun for a person’s utterance and includes recitation, supplication, and conversation; here recitation is especially relevant to the following verses.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p190/r3.anchor: والقول : مصدر ، وهو تلفظ الإنسان بالكلام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p190/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p190/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p190/r4.claim: The conditional apodosis is omitted and supplied by “He knows the secret and what is more hidden”: do not strain yourself, since loud speech has no advantage.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p190/r4.anchor: وجواب شرط { وإن تجهر بالقول } محذوف يدل عليه قوله : { فإنه يعلم السر وأخفى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p190/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p190/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p190/r5.claim: The verse’s main point is not how people should supplicate: the Sunna establishes loud supplication and remembrance, so that issue is relevant here only by implication.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p190/r5.anchor: وبهذا تعلم أن ليس مساق الآية لتعليم الناس كيفية الدعاء ، فقد ثبت في السنة الجهر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p190/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p190/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p190/r6.claim: Akhfā is a comparative with its comparison elided: “more hidden than the secret”; it refers to inner speech and sounds quieter than whispered speech.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p190/r6.anchor: وأخفى اسم تفضيل ، وحذف المفضل عليه لدلالة المقام عليه ، أي وأخفى من السر

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p270#5/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p270#5/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p270#5/r1.claim: To speak aloud is to raise one's voice; Moses need not strain to do so, because God knows even what is secret.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p270#5/r1.anchor: أي ترفع صوتك فانه يعلم السر والمعنى لا تجهد نفسك برفع الصوت فان الله يعلم السر

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p270#5/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p270#5/r2.speaker: جماعة عن ابن عباس والضحاك
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p270#5/r2.claim: One view makes the secret what a person hides within, while ‘more hidden’ is what has not yet happened but will happen; this is transmitted from Ibn Abbas and held by al-Dahhak.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p270#5/r2.anchor: أحدها أن السر ما أسره الإنسان في نفسه وأخفى ما لم يكن بعد وسيكون رواه جماعة عن ابن عباس وبه قال الضحاك

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p270#5/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p270#5/r3.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p270#5/r3.claim: Said ibn Jubayr says the secret is what one says inwardly and ‘more hidden’ is what one has not spoken.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p270#5/r3.anchor: والثاني أن السر ما حدثت به نفسك واخفى ما لم تلفظ به قاله سعيد بن جبير

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p270#5/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p270#5/r4.speaker: مجاهد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p270#5/r4.claim: Mujahid interprets the secret as a deed hidden from other people and what is more hidden as a whisper.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p270#5/r4.anchor: والثالث أن السر العمل الذي يسره الإنسان من الناس وأخفى منه الوسوسة قاله مجاهد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p270#5/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p270#5/r5.speaker: زيد بن أسلم وابنه
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p270#5/r5.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam and his son say God knows His servants' secrets while concealing His own secret from them, so they do not know it.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p270#5/r5.anchor: والرابع أن معنى الكلام يعلم إسرار عباده وقد أخفى سره عنهم فلا يعلم قاله زيد بن أسلم وابنه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p270#5/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p270#5/r6.speaker: الفراء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p270#5/r6.claim: Al-Farraʾ says God knows what a person tells another and what the person hides within himself.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p270#5/r6.anchor: والخامس يعلم ما أسره الإنسان إلى غيره وما أخفاه في نفسه قاله الفراء

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p274#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p274#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p274#2/r1.claim: Ibn Kathir calls the preceding report exceptionally strange and unique to al-Qasim ibn Abd al-Rahman.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p274#2/r1.anchor: هذا حديث غريب جدا، وسياق عجيب، تفرد به القاسم بن عبد الرحمن هذا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p274#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p274#2/r2.speaker: يحيى بن معين
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p274#2/r2.claim: Yahya ibn Ma'in judged al-Qasim ibn Abd al-Rahman worthless as a transmitter.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p274#2/r2.anchor: وقد قال فيه يحيى بن معين: "ليس يساوي شيئا"

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p274#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p274#2/r3.speaker: أبو حاتم الرازي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p274#2/r3.claim: Abu Hatim al-Razi weakened al-Qasim ibn Abd al-Rahman.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p274#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p274#2/r4.speaker: ابن عدي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p274#2/r4.claim: Ibn Adi said al-Qasim ibn Abd al-Rahman was unknown.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p274#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p274#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p274#2/r5.claim: Ibn Kathir says the report muddles material from different reports; the narrator may have done so deliberately or someone may have inserted it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p274#2/r5.anchor: وقد خلط في هذا الحديث، ودخل عليه شيء في شيء، وحديث في حديث

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p274#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p274#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p274#2/r6.claim: God knows the secret and what is still more hidden, so the revelation comes from the Creator who knows all hidden things.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p274#2/r6.anchor: وقوله: {وإن تجهر بالقول فإنه يعلم السر وأخفى} أي: أنزل هذا القرآن

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p274#2/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p274#2/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p274#2/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas says the secret is what a person conceals inwardly, while what is more hidden is what he will do before he knows it; God's knowledge of past and future is one, and creation is like one person to Him.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p274#2/r7.anchor: قال علي بن أبي طلحة، عن ابن عباس: {يعلم السر وأخفى}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p274#2/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p274#2/r8.speaker: الضحاك
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p274#2/r8.claim: Al-Dahhak defines the secret as one's inner self-talk and what is more hidden as thoughts not yet entertained.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p274#2/r8.anchor: وقال الضحاك: {يعلم السر وأخفى} قال: السر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p274#2/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p274#2/r9.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p274#2/r9.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr says people know what they think today but not tomorrow, whereas God knows both today's and tomorrow's thoughts.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p274#2/r9.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير: أنت تعلم ما تسر اليوم، ولا تعلم ما تسر غدا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p274#2/r10.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p274#2/r10.speaker: مجاهد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p274#2/r10.claim: Mujahid interprets what is more hidden as whispering.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p274#2/r11.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p274#2/r11.speaker: مجاهد وسعيد بن جبير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p274#2/r11.claim: Mujahid and Sa'id ibn Jubayr also explain it as what a person will do without having yet thought of it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p274#2/r11.anchor: وقال أيضا هو وسعيد بن جبير: {وأخفى} أي: ما هو عامله

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p54/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p54/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p54/r1.claim: God knows what someone confides to another and what is more hidden: either what the person conceals inwardly or what they will later conceal in themselves.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p54/r1.anchor: أي يعلم ما أسررته إلى غيرك وأخفى من ذلك ، وهو ما أخطرته ببالك

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p54/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p54/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p54/r2.claim: Another view parses أخفى as a verb: God knows people's secrets and what He has kept hidden from them; al-Zamakhsharī rejects this as unconvincing.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p54/r2.anchor: وعن بعضهم : أن أخفى فعل يعنى أنه يعلم أسرار العباد وأخفى عنهم ما يعلمه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p54/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p54/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p54/r3.claim: If the condition means loudly invoking God, the response teaches that He does not need loud speech: it either forbids loudness or teaches that it serves another purpose than making God hear.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p54/r3.anchor: معناه وإن تجهر بذكر الله من دعاء أو غيره فأعلم أنه غني عن جهرك

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p392#2/r22.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p392#2/r22.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p392#2/r22.claim: The question “why speak aloud?” underscores that God knows what is spoken aloud and what is secret.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p392#2/r22.anchor: فم حاجتك إلى الجهر ؟ لأن الله يعلم بالجهر وبالسر

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p392#2/r23.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p392#2/r23.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p392#2/r23.claim: The secret is what a person tells another privately; what is more hidden is what the person keeps within and tells no one.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p392#2/r23.anchor: ما حدث به العبد غيره في السر . ( وأخفى ) ما أضمره في نفسه , ولم يحدث به غيره , قاله ابن عباس

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p392#2/r24.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p392#2/r24.speaker: قتادة وسعيد بن جبير
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p392#2/r24.claim: The secret is an inward thought; what is more hidden is something that has not existed and no one has thought.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p392#2/r24.anchor: أن السر ما أضمره العبد في نفسه . وأخفى منه ما لم يكن ولا أضمره أحد في نفسه قاله قتادة وسعيد بن جبير

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p392#2/r25.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p392#2/r25.speaker: ابن زيد
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p392#2/r25.claim: The secret is the servants' inner thoughts, while what is more hidden is God's own secret from creation.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p392#2/r25.anchor: يعلم أسرار عباده , وأخفى سر نفسه عن خلقه , قاله ابن زيد

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p392#2/r26.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p392#2/r26.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p392#2/r26.claim: The secret is what people conceal, and what is more hidden is whispering.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p392#2/r26.anchor: ما أسره الناس , وأخفى : الوسوسة , قاله مجاهد

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p392#2/r27.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p392#2/r27.speaker: الكلبي
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p392#2/r27.claim: The secret is prior knowledge and deeds; what is more hidden is knowledge of a person's future deeds.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p392#2/r27.anchor: أن السر ما أسره من علمه وعمله السالف , وأخفى : وما يعلمه من عمله المستأنف , وهذا معنى قول الكلبي

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p392#2/r28.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p392#2/r28.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p392#2/r28.claim: The secret may mean resolve, and what is more hidden the impulse below the level of resolve.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p392#2/r28.anchor: السر : العزيمة , وما هو أخفى : هو الهم الذي دون العزيمة

MUJAHID:v1p393#2/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p393#2/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p393#2/r1.claim: The secret is what one conceals from other people; what is more hidden is inner whispering.
MUJAHID:v1p393#2/r1.anchor: ﴿ السر ﴾ الذي تستره من الناس ﴿ وأخفى ﴾ يعني الوسوسة

MUJAHID:v1p394/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p394/r1.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
MUJAHID:v1p394/r1.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr says the secret is what one keeps within oneself, while the more hidden is what one has not yet thought to oneself.
MUJAHID:v1p394/r1.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير في قوله ﴿ يعلم السر وأخفى ﴾ قال السر ما أسررت في نفسك

NASAFI-FULL:v3p50#7/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p50#7/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p50#7/r1.claim: Tajhar means to raise your voice.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p50#7/r1.anchor: ترفع صوتك ﴿ فإنه يعلم السر ﴾ ما أسررته إلى غيرك

NASAFI-FULL:v3p50#7/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p50#7/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p50#7/r2.claim: The sirr is what you disclose privately to another; akhfā is either a thought occurring in your mind or something you will later conceal within yourself.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p50#7/r2.anchor: ما أسررته في نفسك وما ستسره فيها

RAZI-FULL:v22p8/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p8/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p8/r2.claim: After mentioning God's enthronement, the passage follows with power and then knowledge: the ownership statement displays power, and 20:7 displays knowledge.
RAZI-FULL:v22p8/r2.anchor: والملك لا ينتظم إلا بالقدرة والعلم ، لا جرم عقبه بالقدرة ثم بالعلم

RAZI-FULL:v22p8/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p8/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p8/r3.claim: One reading takes أخفى as an intensive or comparative form, dividing what God knows into the spoken aloud, the secret, and the still more hidden.
RAZI-FULL:v22p8/r3.anchor: إن قوله : { وأخفى } بناء المبالغة ، وعلى هذا القول نقول إنه تعالى قسم الأشياء إلى ثلاثة أقسام

RAZI-FULL:v22p8/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p8/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p8/r4.claim: The most evident sense is that the secret and the more hidden are unspoken matters: God knows what cannot be heard, so He certainly knows what is spoken aloud.
RAZI-FULL:v22p8/r4.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون المراد بالسر وبالأخفى ما ليس بقول وهذا أظهر

RAZI-FULL:v22p8/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p8/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p8/r5.claim: Possible meanings of the hidden levels include a resolve concealed within oneself versus a thought not yet resolved, what is resolved versus an unformed notion, or even what has not yet entered the mind; future divine acts are another possibility.
RAZI-FULL:v22p8/r5.anchor: والسر هو الذي يسره المرء في نفسه من الأمور التي عزم عليها ، والأخفى هو الذي لم يبلغ حد العزيمة

RAZI-FULL:v22p8/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p8/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p8/r6.claim: Al-Rāzī's nearest reading confines secret and hidden matters to what warrants reward or punishment, making the verse a warning against inward and outward sins and an encouragement to inward and outward obedience.
RAZI-FULL:v22p8/r6.anchor: والمقصود منه زجر المكلف عن القبائح ظاهرة كانت أو باطنة ، والترغيب في الطاعات ظاهرة كانت أو باطنة

RAZI-FULL:v22p8/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p8/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p8/r7.claim: A second parse reads أخفى as a verb: God knows people's secrets and has concealed from them what He knows.
RAZI-FULL:v22p8/r7.anchor: أن أخفى فعل يعني أنه يعلم أسرار العباد وأخفى عنهم ما يعلمه

RAZI-FULL:v22p8/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p8/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p8/r8.claim: The conditional can mean that God has no need to hear a loud invocation or other mention because He already knows it.
RAZI-FULL:v22p8/r8.anchor: إن تجهر بذكر الله تعالى من دعاء أو غيره ، فاعلم أنه غني عن جهرك

RAZI-FULL:v22p8/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p8/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p8/r9.claim: Alternatively, the verse discourages loud remembrance, as 7:205 instructs worshippers to remember God inwardly, humbly, fearfully, and without loud speech.
RAZI-FULL:v22p8/r9.anchor: وإما أن يكون نهيا عن الجهر كقوله : { واذكر ربك في نفسك تضرعا وخيفة ودون الجهر من القول }

RAZI-FULL:v22p8/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p8/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p8/r10.claim: A further explanation is that loud speech serves some other purpose, since it is not needed for God to hear.
RAZI-FULL:v22p8/r10.anchor: وإما تعليما للعباد أن الجهر ليس لاستماع الله تعالى ، وإنما هو لغرض آخر

RAZI-FULL:v22p8/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p8/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p8/r11.claim: God knows all objects at all times through one unchanging knowledge, an essential attribute of His that is neither originated nor contingent.
RAZI-FULL:v22p8/r11.anchor: وذلك العلم غير متغير ، وذلك العلم من لوازم ذاته من غير أن يكون موصوفا بالحدوث أو الإمكان

RAZI-FULL:v22p8/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p8/r12.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p8/r12.claim: A servant's share in knowledge is less than a speck, yet even that tiny share discloses divine attributes; all knowledge ultimately belongs to God because He teaches it, as 4:166 and 67:14 say.
RAZI-FULL:v22p8/r12.anchor: بل الحق أن الدينار بتمامه له ، لأن الذي علمته فإنما علمته بتعليمه على ما قال : { أنزله بعلمه }

RAZI-FULL:v22p8/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p8/r13.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p8/r13.claim: Like the sun illuminating the world without losing any light, God's imparting knowledge does not diminish His own knowledge; nature also shows His detailed awareness of every particle.
RAZI-FULL:v22p8/r13.anchor: فإن من تدبيراته في خلق الأشجار وأنواع النبات أنها ليس لها فم ولا سائر آلات الغذاء

STUDYQURAN:20:7/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:7/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:20:7/r1.claim: The secret is hidden talk; what is more hidden still is buried deep in the soul and known only to God.
STUDYQURAN:20:7/r1.anchor: What is secret refers to hidden talk (Kl), and what is more hidden still refers

STUDYQURAN:20:7/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:7/r2.speaker: a common Sufi psychological teaching
STUDYQURAN:20:7/r2.claim: In Sufi psychology, sirr is the heart, the locus of awareness of God, while akhfā is a deeper dimension of that same reality.
STUDYQURAN:20:7/r2.anchor: According to a common Sufi psychological teaching, the secret

STUDYQURAN:20:7/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:7/r3.speaker: al-Rāzī
STUDYQURAN:20:7/r3.claim: Al-Rāzī reasons a fortiori that if God knows the innermost thoughts, He also knows what people speak aloud.
STUDYQURAN:20:7/r3.anchor: Al-Rāzī deduces from the second part of this verse that if God knows the innermost recesses of a person’s thoughts

STUDYQURAN:20:7/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:7/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:20:7/r4.claim: Verses 6–7 together resemble 2:284, which says God knows what people disclose or hide in their souls; compare other statements of God's knowledge.
STUDYQURAN:20:7/r4.anchor: Taken together, vv. 6–7 are in part similar to 2:284

SULAMI:v1p435#3/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p435#3/r1.speaker: author
SULAMI:v1p435#3/r1.claim: The secret is an inspiration hidden from the servant's senses, reason, and awareness of angels and devils, lodged in the heart's core until will and decree bring it into manifestation and it moves through states.
SULAMI:v1p435#3/r1.anchor: قال : السر ما يطالعه العبد ، ولا يطالعه الملك

SULAMI:v1p435#3/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p435#3/r2.speaker: author
SULAMI:v1p435#3/r2.claim: What is more hidden has not yet appeared and is known only to God; when its concealment is disclosed, its action begins.
SULAMI:v1p435#3/r2.anchor: وما هو أخفى فما لم يحن ولم يطالع لا يعلمه إلا الله

SULAMI:v1p435#3/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p435#3/r3.speaker: الواسطي
