SULAMI:v1p435#3/r3.claim: Al-Wasiti says the secret is what creatures do not know, and the more hidden is what God has not yet commanded to exist.
SULAMI:v1p435#3/r3.anchor: وقال الواسطي رحمه الله : السر ما خفي على العباد

SULAMI:v1p435#3/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p435#3/r4.speaker: الفضيل بن عياض
SULAMI:v1p435#3/r4.claim: Al-Fudayl interprets God's knowledge of the secret and what is more hidden as knowledge of what is in a person's self and what that person will know tomorrow.
SULAMI:v1p435#3/r4.anchor: سمعت الفضيل بن عياض يقول : في قوله : ﴿ يعلم السر

SULAMI:v1p435#3/r5.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p435#3/r5.speaker: الجنيد
SULAMI:v1p435#3/r5.claim: Junayd says God knows His secret within a person and the more hidden secret within that person.
SULAMI:v1p435#3/r5.anchor: قال الجنيد رحمه الله : يعلم سره فيك وأخفى سره

TUSTARI:20:7/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:20:7/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:20:7/r1.claim: What is more hidden than a secret is a thought the servant has not yet entertained, which comes to mind in sleep.
TUSTARI:20:7/r1.anchor: أخفى من السر ما لم يفكره العبد فيه وهو مفكره نوما

TABRISI:20:1-2/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:1-2/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:1-2/r8.claim: Jahr means raising the voice; the source gives verb and participial forms and contrasts it with hushed speech.
TABRISI:20:1-2/r8.anchor: والجهر رفع الصوت يقال جهر يجهر جهرا فهو جاهر والصوت مجهور وضده المهموس

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p277#3/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p277#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p277#3/r1.claim: Al-sirr is what a person keeps secret and does not disclose.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p277#3/r1.anchor: يعلم السر} ما أسررته ولم تظهره.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p277#3/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p277#3/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p277#3/r2.claim: Akhfā refers to what a person has only told himself.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p357/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p357/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p357/r1.claim: The wording is an unusual contrast: one might expect the condition to say that God knows the secret if one speaks privately.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p357/r1.anchor: وكان من حق المقابلة أن يقول

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p357/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p357/r2.speaker: المفضل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p357/r2.claim: Al-Mufaddal understands loud recitation: there is no need to strain by raising the voice, since God knows even what is kept unspoken.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p357/r2.anchor: فقال المفضل: ({وإن تجهر بالقول} أي: ترفع صوتك بالقراءة {فإنه يعلم السر وأخفى} فلا تجهد نفسك

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p357/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p357/r3.speaker: صاحب النظم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p357/r3.claim: The نظم author says that if God knows what is secret and still more hidden, then He certainly knows what is spoken aloud.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p357/r3.anchor: وقال صاحب النظم: (معناه وإن تجهر بالقول فتظهره] (¬5) فهو يعلم # السر وأخفى منه فكيف الجهر)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p357/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p357/r4.speaker: صاحب النظم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p357/r4.claim: The نظم author also reads an ellipsis: whether one speaks openly or not, God knows the secret and what is still more hidden, so speaking aloud is unnecessary.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p357/r4.anchor: وذكر وجها آخر وهو: أن يكون في الكلام اختصار

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p357/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p357/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p357/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas, in the report through Saʿid ibn Jubayr, says the secret is what a person knows and conceals, while the more hidden is what has not yet occurred but will.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p357/r5.anchor: قال ابن عباس فيما روى عنه سعيد بن جبير: (السر ما علمت أنت مما أسررت في نفسك،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p357/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p357/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p357/r6.claim: In the al-Walibi report, Ibn Abbas says God knows what people hide and what they will do before they know it, with one knowledge encompassing past and future.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p357/r6.anchor: وقال في رواية الوالبي: (السر: ما أسر ابن آدم في نفسه، وأخفى: ما خفي على ابن آدم مما هو فاعله قبل أن يعلمه،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p357/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p357/r7.speaker: مجاهد وقتادة وسفيان والضحاك وسعيد بن جبير
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p357/r7.claim: Mujahid, Qatada, Sufyan, al-Dahhak, and Saʿid ibn Jubayr share Ibn Abbas’s view that God knows future acts before people know them.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p357/r7.anchor: فيعلمه فيما مضى من ذلك وما بقي علم واحد) (¬3). وهو قول مجاهد، وقتادة، وسفيان، والضحاك، وسعيد بن جبير

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p357/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p357/r8.speaker: أكثرهم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p357/r8.claim: Most commentators say the secret is what one conceals within oneself, and the more hidden is what one has not yet thought of but will happen tomorrow.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p357/r8.anchor: وأكثرهم قالوا: (السر ما أسره في نفسه، وأخفى: ما لم يحدث به نفسه مما يكون في غد)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p359/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p359/r1.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p359/r1.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam says God knows people’s secrets and has concealed His own secret from them, so they cannot know it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p359/r1.anchor: وقال زيد بن أسلم في قوله: {يعلم السر وأخفى}: (يعلم أسرار العباد، وأخفى سره عنهم فلا يعلم)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p359/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p359/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p359/r2.claim: On Zayd’s reading, akhfā derives from concealment and needs no omitted comparison; on the earlier reading it is comparative, derived from hiddenness.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p359/r2.anchor: فعلى هذا لا يحتاج إلى تقدير محذوف؛ لأن أخفى على هذا القول أفعل من الإخفاء. وعلى القول الأول أفعل من الخفاء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p359/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p359/r3.speaker: قوم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p359/r3.claim: Some take akhfā to mean simply “hidden”; the elative form can occur without comparison, as in a poet’s use of awḥad for “one.”
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p359/r3.anchor: وذهب قوم إلى أن (أخفى) هاهنا بمعنى الخفي، وأفعل يأتي في الكلام ولا يراد به التفضيل. كقول الشاعر:

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p359/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p359/r4.speaker: الشاعر
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p359/r4.claim: The cited poet’s word awḥad means “one,” supporting non-comparative use of the elative form.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p359/r4.anchor: تمنى رجال أن أموت وإن أمت ... فتلك سبيل لست فيها بأوحد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p359/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p359/r5.speaker: أبو عبيدة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p359/r5.claim: Abu Ubayda says the Farazdaq’s “more noble and taller” can mean simply “noble and tall,” not comparative.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p359/r5.anchor: وقيل في بيت الفرزدق: إن قوله: أعز وأطول؛ بمعنى: عزيزة طويلة، وهذا قول أبي عبيدة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p359/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p359/r6.speaker: ابن الأنباري
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p359/r6.claim: Ibn al-Anbari rejects this non-comparative reading as contrary to transmitted reports and grammatically remote without necessity; transmitted evidence should prevail.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p359/r6.anchor: قال ابن الأنباري: (وهذا القول يخالف الآثار, ويبعد متناوله عند أهل النحو

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p359/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p359/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p359/r7.claim: The author prefers the interpretations followed by the commentators, rather than treating akhfā as a non-comparative adjective.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p359/r7.anchor: والأولى من هذه الأقاويل ما عليه المفسرون

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:6-7/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:6-7/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:6-7/r2.claim: The secret is what a person hides within themself.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:6-7/r2.anchor: { وإن تجهر بالقول فإنه يعلم السر } وهو ما أسررت لفي نفسك

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:6-7/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:6-7/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:6-7/r3.claim: The more hidden thing is a future thought not yet had; if God knows that, He certainly knows what is spoken aloud.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:6-7/r3.anchor: { وأخفى } وهو ما ستحدث به نفسك مما لم يكن بعد، والمعنى: إنه يعلم هذا، فكيف ما جهر به؟

MAJAZ:v2p16/r1.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p16/r1.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p16/r1.claim: Akhfā is what a person has told only themself and hidden from everyone; afʿal can stand where an active participle is expected, as in the poem’s awḥad.
MAJAZ:v2p16/r1.anchor: فإنه يعلم السر وأخفى» (7) يعنى والخفى الذي حدثت به نفسك ولم تسره إلى أحد

MAJAZ:v2p16/r2.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p16/r2.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p16/r2.claim: Another analysis supplies an ellipsis: ‘He knows the secret and what is more hidden than the secret.’
MAJAZ:v2p16/r2.anchor: وله موضع آخر من المختصر الذي فيه ضمير يعلم السر وأخفى من السر.

BAQILLANI:v1p26/r1.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p26/r1.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p26/r1.claim: The Prophet knew the Qur'an was inimitable as soon as it was revealed, either directly or because he was told it was a proof of his prophethood, before reciting it to others.
BAQILLANI:v1p26/r1.anchor: فصح من هذا الوجه أن النبي حين أوحى إليه القرآن عرف كونه معجزا أو عرف بأن قيل له إنه دلالة وعلم على نبوتك

BAQILLANI:v1p26/r2.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p26/r2.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p26/r2.claim: An eloquence expert recognizes that neither he nor comparable speakers can produce the Qur'an, because it has no counterpart in customary styles; this differs from ordinary poetic skill.
BAQILLANI:v1p26/r2.anchor: متى سمع القرآن عرف أنه معجز لأنه يعرف من حال نفسه أنه لا يقدر عليه وهو يعرف من حال غيره مثل ما يعرف من حال نفسه

BAQILLANI:v1p26/r3.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p26/r3.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p26/r3.claim: Unlike a plainly observable miracle such as the sea parting, recognizing Qur'anic inimitability requires weighing premises and styles, though it ultimately establishes the same miraculous status.
BAQILLANI:v1p26/r3.anchor: فإن النظر في معرفة إعجاز القرآن يحتاج إلى تأمل ويفتقر إلى مراعاة مقدمات والكشف عن أمور

BAQILLANI:v1p259/r1.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p259/r1.speaker: أبو الحسن الأشعري
BAQILLANI:v1p259/r1.claim: Al-Ashʿari holds that the Qur'an's appearance through the Prophet is known necessarily, while its status as a miracle is established by inference.
BAQILLANI:v1p259/r1.anchor: ذهب الشيخ أبو الحسن الأشعري إلى أن ظهور ذلك عن النبي يعلم ضرورة وكونه معجزا يعلم باستدلال

BAQILLANI:v1p259/r2.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p259/r2.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p259/r2.claim: Non-Arabs and non-eloquent listeners can know the Qur'an's inimitability only by inference; a master of Arabic rhetoric knows his own incapacity necessarily, then infers others' incapacity.
BAQILLANI:v1p259/r2.anchor: والذي نقوله في هذا إن الأعجمي لا يمكنه أن يعلم إعجازه إلا استدلالا وكذلك من لم يكن بليغا

BURHAN:v3p253/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p253/r1.speaker: ابن عباس وغيره
BURHAN:v3p253/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and others explain secret as what one conceals within oneself and more hidden as what has not yet occurred to one’s mind; both are equally known to God.
BURHAN:v3p253/r1.anchor: فعن ابن عباس وغيره السر ما أسررت في نفسك وأخفى منه ما لم تحدث به نفسك مما يكون

BURHAN:v3p253/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p253/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p253/r2.claim: The wording with more hidden is more emphatic; one analysis treats it as a comparative requiring an understood comparison, while another says it observes the verse endings.
BURHAN:v3p253/r2.anchor: ولا شك أن الآتي أبلغ وفيه وجهان أحدهما أنه أفعل تفضيل يستدعي مفضلا عليه علم

BURHAN:v3p285/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p285/r7.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p285/r7.claim: Although secret and more hidden reverses the usual order that would put hidden knowledge last, the verse does so to preserve the rhyme of its endings.

ITQAN:v4p324#3/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p324#3/r1.speaker: أبو الحسن الأشعري
ITQAN:v4p324#3/r1.claim: Al-Ash'ari holds that the Qur'an's appearance as a miracle to the Prophet is known necessarily, while its being inimitable is known by inference.
ITQAN:v4p324#3/r1.anchor: فذهب أبو الحسن الأشعري إلى أن ظهور ذلك على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يعلم ضرورة وكونه معجزا يعلم بالاستدلال

ITQAN:v4p324#3/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p324#3/r2.speaker: القاضي
ITQAN:v4p324#3/r2.claim: Al-Qadi says non-Arabic speakers and non-eloquent people can know the Qur'an's inimitability only by inference; an eloquent person versed in Arab styles necessarily senses his own and others' inability to match it.
ITQAN:v4p324#3/r2.anchor: والذي نقوله إن الأعجمي لا يمكنه أن يعلم إعجازه إلا استدلالا وكذلك من ليس ببليغ فأما البليغ الذي قد أحاط بمذاهب العرب وغرائب الصنعة

BURHAN:v3p230/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p230/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p230/r6.claim: أخفى includes what has not entered conscious thought as inner promptings, beyond what has occurred to the heart as imagined whispers.
BURHAN:v3p230/r6.anchor: أي وهو مالم يقع في وهم الضمير من الهواجس ولم يخطر على القلوب من مخيلات الوساوس

BURHAN:v4p170/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p170/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p170/r2.claim: The thing being compared may be omitted, and afعل can occur outside a predicate position, as in يعلم السر وأخفى.
BURHAN:v4p170/r2.anchor: وقد يحذف المفضول و افعل ليس بخبر

BURHAN:v3p152/r11.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p152/r11.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p152/r11.claim: The same ellipsis is illustrated by “He knows the secret and what is more hidden than the secret.”
BURHAN:v3p152/r11.anchor: ﴿ فإنه يعلم السر وأخفى ﴾ 2 أي من السر

ITQAN:v3p35/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p35/r6.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p35/r6.claim: The unseen precedes the witnessed because it is more exalted, while “secret and more hidden” reverses the sequence to maintain the verse ending.
ITQAN:v3p35/r6.anchor: ومنه تقديم الغيب على الشهادة في قوله ﴿ عالم الغيب والشهادة ﴾ لأن علمه أشرف

ITQAN:v3p268/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p268/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p268/r2.claim: A comparative can omit what it is being compared with: 'knows the secret and what is more hidden' and 'better and more enduring.'
ITQAN:v3p268/r2.anchor: ومنه حذف متعلق أفعل التفضيل نحو ﴿ يعلم السر وأخفى ﴾ ﴿ خير وأبقى ﴾
